_readme: Verification record for every scripture citation in src/data/content. Each hadith was opened at sunnah.com under the number the content cites, because that is the numbering this project uses; cross-numbered editions of Sunan Abi Dawud in particular do not line up. Quran citations were read from the Saheeh International edition through AlQuran Cloud. npm run verify:citations gates the build on every citation having an entry and every entry still being cited.

Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1078.confirmedWording: The believer's soul is suspended by his debt until it is settled for him

Jami' at-Tirmidhi 31.confirmedWording: the Prophet would go through his beard
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 31.note: Covers the beard alone. Running water between the fingers and toes is cited to Sunan Abi Dawud 142.

Quran 16:98.confirmedWording: when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the expelled

Quran 22:77.confirmedWording: bow and prostrate and worship your Lord

Quran 2:144.confirmedWording: So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram

Quran 2:222.confirmedWording: do not approach them until they are pure

Quran 2:238.confirmedWording: Maintain with care the obligatory prayers

Quran 4:101.confirmedWording: there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer

Quran 4:103.confirmedWording: prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times

Quran 5:6.confirmedWording: wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows and wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles

Quran 62:9.confirmedWording: when the adhan is called for the prayer on the day of Jumu'ah

Quran 7:31.confirmedWording: take your adornment at every masjid

Sahih Bukhari 1.confirmedWording: The reward of deeds depends upon the intentions
Sahih Bukhari 1.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 1081.narrator: Anas ibn Malik, reported by Yahya ibn Ishaq
Sahih Bukhari 1081.confirmedWording: we travelled with the Prophet from Medina to Mecca and offered two rakaat for every prayer
Sahih Bukhari 1081.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Bukhari 1081.note: Records a journey on which the prayer was shortened. The thresholds of distance and duration are inferences the schools differ over, which the item now says.

Sahih Bukhari 1090.confirmedWording: the prayer in a journey was kept as it was, the prayers for non-travellers were completed
Sahih Bukhari 1090.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Bukhari 1090.note: Establishes the shortening of the four-unit prayers. That Maghrib stays three is by established practice.

Sahih Bukhari 1224.confirmedWording: got up for the third rakah without sitting, then made the two corrective prostrations before the tasleem
Sahih Bukhari 1224.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 1226.confirmedWording: offered five rakaat in the Zuhr prayer, then made two prostrations of sahw after the tasleem
Sahih Bukhari 1226.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 1245.confirmedWording: went to the Musalla, the people stood behind him in rows, and he said four takbirs
Sahih Bukhari 1245.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Bukhari 1245.note: Describes standing in rows and the takbirs. That the prayer has no bowing and no prostration is agreed upon, which the item now says.

Sahih Bukhari 1253.confirmedWording: Wash her thrice or five times or more, if you see it necessary
Sahih Bukhari 1253.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Bukhari 1253.note: Permits three, five, or more. It does not itself mandate an odd count, nor does it cover who may wash whom.

Sahih Bukhari 1264.confirmedWording: shrouded in three white Yemeni cotton cloths, with neither shirt nor turban
Sahih Bukhari 1264.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 1265.confirmedWording: the man who died in ihram at Arafat: wash him, shroud him, do not perfume him, do not cover his head
Sahih Bukhari 1265.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 1294.confirmedWording: He who slaps his cheeks and tears his clothes is not one of us
Sahih Bukhari 1294.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 1315.confirmedWording: Hurry up with the dead body
Sahih Bukhari 1315.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Bukhari 1315.note: Commands haste. Laying the body on its right side facing the qibla is the agreed practice, which the item now says.

Sahih Bukhari 1335.confirmedWording: Ibn Abbas recited Al-Fatiha in the funeral prayer and said it is the Sunnah
Sahih Bukhari 1335.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 1346.confirmedWording: Bury them with their blood, said of the dead of Uhud, and he did not have them washed
Sahih Bukhari 1346.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 135.confirmedWording: The prayer of a person who does hadath is not accepted till he performs ablution
Sahih Bukhari 135.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 159.confirmedWording: poured water over his hands and washed them thrice, rinsed his mouth and nose, washed each limb thrice
Sahih Bukhari 159.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 168.confirmedWording: used to like to start from the right side on wearing shoes, combing his hair and cleaning himself
Sahih Bukhari 168.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Bukhari 168.note: A general principle rather than a wudu-specific narration. It is the standard evidence for beginning with the right.

Sahih Bukhari 248.confirmedWording: started by washing his hands, performed ablution as for prayer, then poured water over his head
Sahih Bukhari 248.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 249.confirmedWording: washed off the discharge from his private parts, then poured water over his body
Sahih Bukhari 249.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 282.confirmedWording: a woman takes a bath if she notices a discharge after a wet dream
Sahih Bukhari 282.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 320.confirmedWording: give up the prayers when the menses begin, and when it has finished take a bath and start praying
Sahih Bukhari 320.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 321.confirmedWording: he never ordered us to make up the prayers missed in menstruation
Sahih Bukhari 321.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Bukhari 321.note: Covers prayer only. The fasting make-up rule is cited to Sahih Muslim 335.

Sahih Bukhari 3370.narrator: Ka'b ibn Ujrah, reported by Abdur-Rahman ibn Abi Layla
Sahih Bukhari 3370.confirmedWording: Allahumma salli ala Muhammad wa ala aali Muhammad
Sahih Bukhari 3370.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 347.narrator: Ammar ibn Yasir, reported by Shaqiq
Sahih Bukhari 347.confirmedWording: struck the earth with his hands, passed them over each other, then wiped his face
Sahih Bukhari 347.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 597.confirmedWording: If anyone forgets a prayer he should pray that prayer when he remembers it
Sahih Bukhari 597.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 598.confirmedWording: on the day of al-Khandaq he prayed Asr after sunset and then prayed Maghrib
Sahih Bukhari 598.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Bukhari 598.note: The order of the make-up rests on this sequence: the missed Asr was prayed before the current Maghrib.

Sahih Bukhari 6251.confirmedWording: perform the ablution properly, face the Qibla, and say the Takbir
Sahih Bukhari 6251.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 631.confirmedWording: Pray as you have seen me praying
Sahih Bukhari 631.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 735.confirmedWording: raised both hands on opening the prayer, on the takbir for bowing, and on rising from bowing
Sahih Bukhari 735.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 740.confirmedWording: The people were ordered to place the right hand on the left forearm in the prayer
Sahih Bukhari 740.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Bukhari 740.note: The narration says the forearm. Where the hands rest is a point the schools differ on, which the item now says.

Sahih Bukhari 744.confirmedWording: used to keep silent between the Takbir and the recitation for a short interval
Sahih Bukhari 744.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 756.confirmedWording: Whoever does not recite Al-Fatiha in his prayer, his prayer is invalid
Sahih Bukhari 756.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 776.narrator: Abdullah ibn Abi Qatadah, from his father
Sahih Bukhari 776.confirmedWording: used to recite Al-Fatiha followed by another surah in the first two rakaat
Sahih Bukhari 776.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 782.confirmedWording: Say Amen when the Imam says ghayri l-maghdubi alayhim wa la d-dalleen
Sahih Bukhari 782.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 789.confirmedWording: said Takbir on starting and on bowing, then Sami Allahu liman hamidah on rising
Sahih Bukhari 789.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 793.confirmedWording: the man told to go back and pray, then taught to bow, rise, and prostrate with calmness
Sahih Bukhari 793.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 795.confirmedWording: when he said Sami Allahu liman hamidah he would say Rabbana wa laka l-hamd
Sahih Bukhari 795.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 8.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 812.confirmedWording: I have been ordered to prostrate on seven bones
Sahih Bukhari 812.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 829.confirmedWording: stood after the second rakah without sitting, then made the two corrective prostrations
Sahih Bukhari 829.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Bukhari 829.note: The proof that the first tashahhud is an obligatory duty and not a pillar: leaving it is repaired by the prostration of forgetfulness.

Sahih Bukhari 831.narrator: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, reported by Shaqiq ibn Salamah
Sahih Bukhari 831.confirmedWording: at-Tahiyyatu lillahi wa s-salawatu wa t-tayyibat
Sahih Bukhari 831.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 877.confirmedWording: Anyone of you attending the Friday prayers should take a bath
Sahih Bukhari 877.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Bukhari 877.note: Names the bath. Clean clothes, fragrance, and arriving early rest on other reports, which the item now says.

Sahih Bukhari 887.confirmedWording: I would have ordered them to clean their teeth with siwak for every prayer
Sahih Bukhari 887.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Bukhari 934.confirmedWording: when the Imam is delivering the Khutba and you tell your companion to be quiet, you have done an evil act
Sahih Bukhari 934.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 1631.confirmedWording: when a man dies his acts come to an end but three: recurring charity, knowledge people benefit from, and a pious child who prays for him
Sahih Muslim 1631.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 225.narrator: Abu Hurayrah, reported by Hammam ibn Munabbih
Sahih Muslim 225.confirmedWording: the prayer of one of you is not accepted in a state of impurity until he performs ablution
Sahih Muslim 225.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 226.confirmedWording: washed his hands thrice, rinsed mouth and nose, washed the face three times, the right arm then the left, wiped the head, the right foot then the left
Sahih Muslim 226.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 226.note: Establishes the order of the acts. Continuity between them is the inference of the jurists, not a wording in this narration.

Sahih Muslim 234.confirmedWording: whoever performs the ablution well and then testifies, the eight gates of Paradise are opened for him
Sahih Muslim 234.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 335.confirmedWording: we were ordered to complete the fasts, but were not ordered to complete the prayers
Sahih Muslim 335.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 348.confirmedWording: When a man has sexual intercourse bathing becomes obligatory, even if there is no emission
Sahih Muslim 348.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 348.note: Replaced Sahih Muslim 343, which teaches the opposite rule and is held by the majority to be abrogated.

Sahih Muslim 373.confirmedWording: The Messenger of Allah used to remember Allah at all moments
Sahih Muslim 373.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 373.note: Establishes that remembrance is open in every state. Reading a translation is the extension the jurists draw from it.

Sahih Muslim 401.confirmedWording: raised his hands at the beginning of the prayer, then placed his right hand over his left hand
Sahih Muslim 401.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 482.confirmedWording: The nearest a servant comes to his Lord is when he is prostrating, so make supplication
Sahih Muslim 482.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 482.note: Concerns nearness and supplication in prostration, not the words said there. Those are cited to Sahih Muslim 772.

Sahih Muslim 537.confirmedWording: talking to persons is not fitting during the prayer
Sahih Muslim 537.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 537.note: Concerns speech only. Eating, drinking, and excessive movement are cited to scholarly consensus.

Sahih Muslim 571.confirmedWording: cast aside the doubt, build on what he is sure of, then make two prostrations
Sahih Muslim 571.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 580.confirmedWording: raised his right finger, the one next to the thumb, and supplicated with it
Sahih Muslim 580.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 582.narrator: Amir ibn Sa'd, from his father
Sahih Muslim 582.confirmedWording: pronouncing the taslim on his right and on his left until the whiteness of his cheek was seen
Sahih Muslim 582.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 612.confirmedWording: the time windows for Fajr, Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha
Sahih Muslim 612.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 705.confirmedWording: observed the noon and afternoon prayers together, and the sunset and Isha prayers together
Sahih Muslim 705.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 772.confirmedWording: in bowing Subhana Rabbiyal-Azim, and in prostration Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la
Sahih Muslim 772.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 772.note: Carries both formulas in one narration, which is why the obligatory duties and the prostration step were moved to it from Sunan Abi Dawud 869 (graded da'if).

Sahih Muslim 861.confirmedWording: delivered the sermon standing, then sat, then stood for the second sermon
Sahih Muslim 861.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 8a.narrator: Umar ibn al-Khattab, reported by Yahya ibn Ya'mur
Sahih Muslim 8a.confirmedWording: faith in Allah, His angels, His Books, His Messengers, the Last Day, and the Divine Decree
Sahih Muslim 8a.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 916.confirmedWording: Exhort to recite there is no god but Allah to those of you who are dying
Sahih Muslim 916.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 918.confirmedWording: We belong to Allah and to Him shall we return, O Allah reward me for my affliction
Sahih Muslim 918.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 920.confirmedWording: he closed the eyes of Abu Salamah and said, when the soul is taken away the sight follows it
Sahih Muslim 920.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sahih Muslim 963.narrator: Awf ibn Malik, reported by Jubayr ibn Nufayr
Sahih Muslim 963.confirmedWording: O Allah, forgive him, have mercy upon him, give him peace and absolve him
Sahih Muslim 963.grade: the collection carries no grading line
Sahih Muslim 963.note: Preserves the supplication. Placing it after the third takbir is the arrangement the schools agree on, which the item now says. Cited at sunnah.com as 963a and 963b.

Sahih Muslim 976.confirmedWording: I sought permission from Him to visit her grave, and He granted it to me
Sahih Muslim 976.grade: the collection carries no grading line

Sunan Abu Dawud 101.confirmedWording: the ablution of a person who does not mention the name of Allah is not valid

Sunan Abu Dawud 142.confirmedWording: Perform the ablution in full, run the fingers between the fingers, and snuff water well unless you are fasting

Sunan Abu Dawud 203.confirmedWording: The eyes are the leather strap of the anus, so one who sleeps should perform ablution
Sunan Abu Dawud 203.note: Establishes that sleep breaks the ablution. That light dozing while seated does not is the qualification the jurists draw.

Sunan Abu Dawud 311.confirmedWording: the woman with postnatal bleeding would refrain from prayer for forty days

Sunan Abu Dawud 3221.confirmedWording: Seek forgiveness for your brother, and beg steadfastness for him, for he will be questioned now
Sunan Abu Dawud 3221.note: Restored from Sunan Abi Dawud 3215, which in this numbering is the Uhud burial and not Uthman's report.

Sunan Abu Dawud 332.confirmedWording: clean earth is ablution for a Muslim even for ten years, but when you find water let it touch your skin

Sunan Abu Dawud 355.confirmedWording: he came intending to embrace Islam and was commanded to bathe

Sunan Abu Dawud 61.confirmedWording: The key to prayer is purification, its beginning is takbir and its end is taslim

Sunan Abu Dawud 775.confirmedWording: Subhanaka Allahumma wa bihamdika wa tabaraka smuka wa ta'ala jadduka wa la ilaha ghayruk

Sunan Abu Dawud 874.confirmedWording: and between the two prostrations he said, my Lord forgive me

Sunan an-Nasa'i 102.confirmedWording: he wiped his head and his ears, the inside with his forefinger and the outside with his thumbs
Sunan an-Nasa'i 102.note: Replaced Sunan Abi Dawud 134, which carries the same act but is graded da'if.

Sunan an-Nasa'i 1194.narrator: a companion of the Prophet, reported by Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah
Sunan an-Nasa'i 1194.confirmedWording: if any one of you is praying, let him not lift his gaze to the sky
Sunan an-Nasa'i 1194.note: Forbids raising the gaze. It says nothing about the place of prostration, so the item was reworded to what it states.

Sunan an-Nasa'i 1989.confirmedWording: recite Umm al-Qur'an quietly in the first takbir, then say three more takbirs, and the taslim after the last one
Sunan an-Nasa'i 1989.note: States the recitation and the closing taslim. It does not mention blessings upon the Prophet after the second takbir, which is cited to scholarly consensus.
